analysis: Examined both workflow excerpts against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. The visible change adds per-environment opt-in release metadata: .github/workflows/release-provider.yml head lines 298–308 enable CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND only for publishing runs and the matching environment's repository variable. This does not visibly alter signing, credential scope, source verification, or serving authorization. Head lines 143–174 retain source verification before downstream jobs; lines 269–275 require successful build/qualification or the resume path before signing. BASE lines 1093–1104 and 1208–1236 show exact artifact ID/digest downloads followed by staging and coordinator registration; those surrounding steps are outside the mapped changed BASE range. No concrete regression is supported by these units. Relevant contracts are A-005/A-011 release registration authority, A-017/T-054 signed-artifact qualification, and TB-011/T-052 separation of release evidence from serving permission. No visible cache, prompt encryption, billing, logout, or privileged-helper control changes affect the other indexed threats, including T-041. Integration must examine the remaining workflow changes at head lines 941–1023 and 1078–1088 and their scripts: verify cluster facts bind to the final signed artifact, enabled computation failures block publication, disabled failures cannot silently change existing release identity, and downstream consumers do not treat runtime facts as attestation or authorization. Those implementations and coordinator acceptance semantics are not supplied here; uncertainty is a coverage limit, not a finding.
